accuracy.evidence: Every number is computed in the lab from Math.pow and nCr rather than typed, and the lesson's quoted values were checked by script: 1.02¹⁰ = 1.2189944, partial sums 1, 1.2, 1.218, 1.21896 (error 3.44 × 10⁻⁵, correct to 4 d.p. after four terms); 0.98⁶ = 0.8858424, four alternating terms 0.88584; 2.01⁵ = 32.8080401 vs 32(1 + 0.025 + 0.00025) = 32.808; 1.01¹⁰ = 1.1046221 vs 1.1045; the 3-term error for (1 + x)¹⁰ is 0.557% at x = 0.04 and 1.006% at x = 0.05, so the task answer x = 0.04 is right; 120(0.4)³ = 7.68; ²⁰C₃ = 1140. The term ratio T(k+1)/T(k) = (n − k)x/(k + 1) is exact, and for n = 10, k = 2 it is 8x/3 as the lab states. Expansion facts follow the AQA and Edexcel A-level Maths specifications (binomial expansion, positive integer n). Parameterised answers checked at corners: p2 1 + nk/100 (k 1..9, n 2..8, tolerance 0.0005), p4 n(n−1)/2, m3 1 − n/100, m6 n(n−1)(n−2)/6.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented A-level slips for this skill: using the whole number as x (pick-step distractors (1 + 0.997)⁸ and (1 + 1.05)⁷, tag 'xval', m1), a decimal-place slip in x (tag 'dec', (1 − 0.03)⁸), losing the sign of odd powers when x < 0 (step 3 prediction and the sign-flip task, tag 'sign', p3), not raising the factored-out constant to the power (2(1 + 0.005)⁵, tag 'factor', m2), dividing the small part wrongly (2⁵(1 + 0.01)⁵, tag 'half'), thinking larger coefficients make later terms bigger (step 1 prediction 'Bigger, because 120 > 10', tag 'coef', m4), stopping without checking the next term (tag 'stop', m7) and trusting the method for large x (step 5 prediction, tag 'big', m5).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagbapx is about approximation and accuracy, not building expansions: log-scale term-size bars against a 0.001 threshold, a running partial sum with a live calculator value and error, sign chips for a negative x, a choose-the-form task for three specific numbers with slip-specific rejections, and a draggable x on a graph of (1 + x)¹⁰ against its quadratic truncation with a live percentage error and next-term estimate. flagbexp (choosing terms from brackets and coefficients) and the Pascal and permutation labs do none of this, and the 6-shingle gate is under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner finds each idea before it is stated: they must move x down until every bar after x² turns green below the 0.001 line (and see it fail at 0.05); the error readout turns green and the 4 d.p. comparison ticks only when the 4th term is added; the 4-term sum matches 0.98⁶ only once the odd-power signs are negative; wrong forms are rejected with the specific slip named; and they discover 0.04 as the 1% boundary by dragging, with the next-term estimate shown alongside the true error.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: the x³ term 'Bigger, because 120 > 10' (bars show it is about 1/200 of the x term), 1.02¹⁰ 'Smaller' than 1.2 (every added term is positive and the sum grows past 1.2), the x² term of (1 − 0.02)⁶ 'Negative, because of the minus' (making it negative breaks the 4 d.p. match), and a 3-term estimate of 1.3¹⁰ 'Under 1%' (the graph shows about 42%, far over 20%).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Nine feedback messages keyed to the slip: 'xval' (x is the small part added to 1), 'dec' (one decimal place makes x ten times too big), 'power' (the index stays 7), 'factor' (raise the 2 to the 5th), 'half' (divide the small part by the factor), 'sign' (odd powers of negative x are negative), 'coef' (terms shrink because powers of x shrink, not coefficients), 'big' (left-out terms exceed the kept ones at x = 0.5) and 'stop' (the error is about the first omitted term, 45x² = 0.0045).

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes the learner limits (kid FK ≤ 6.5 + 0.5, adult ≤ 9.5 + 0.5). Kid paragraphs use short sentences around one worked number each (1.02¹⁰, 0.997⁸, 2.01⁵, 0.98⁶) and the precise terms of the topic: expansion, coefficient, term, power, error, decimal places. Canvas text is 13–19 px with term captions such as ¹⁰C₂·0.02² under each value.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes (no banned phrases, explanation overlap under 12% against the existing binomial lessons). Each kid paragraph carries one idea (terms shrink with a worked sum; why, via the term ratio; rewriting into a(1 + x)ⁿ and signs; judging accuracy by the first omitted term); adult paragraphs give the ratio result, checked worked values, six named mistakes and what the lab does.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at iPhone 13 (390 px) in both themes after Show me on every step. Fixes made from them: the six term chips in one row overflowed with values like 0.0000336, so chips are now two rows of three with the term caption inside; the 0.001 threshold label collided with the x track labels and moved below the bars; value labels inside long bars were clipped and are now right-aligned inside the bar, using dark ink on the light dark-theme bar colour; the graph legend moved off the dashed x line. Buttons wrap two per row with no clipping.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button: Smaller x/Bigger x, Add the next term, Flip x¹–x⁴ sign (aria-labels name the power), one button per candidate expansion, and x − 0.01/x + 0.01 for the graph; the challenge uses buttons. tell() updates the canvas aria-label and visible description with the full numeric state (sum, true value, error). walk.cjs on desktop and iPhone 13 completed all 5 tasks with Show me, showed the challenge, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) found no violations in either theme and no console errors.
